issues.location: compiled.selectors[0] / cards[0]['Identifying paths'] (focal + auxiliary paths for obligation workspaces_with_oncall_admin)
issues.problem: The binding_note requires that the SAME user who is a member of the workspace's on-call channel also holds an admin WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP record for that SAME workspace ('the same user's workspace-membership record for that same workspace must show an admin role'). The compiled query does not encode this equality. The focal path (teams->channels->channel_members->users->user_teams) joins on user_id only and filters user_teams.role='admin' with no constraint that user_teams.team_id equals the root teams.team_id — so it matches if the on-call member holds admin ANYWHERE, in any workspace. The auxiliary path (teams->user_teams via team_id, role='admin') independently checks only that the root workspace has SOME admin, without tying that admin back to the specific on-call channel member found by the focal path. Combining these two independent existence checks does not reconstruct the intended single relational condition; they are logically distinct claims ('some on-call member is admin somewhere' AND 'this workspace has some admin, possibly a different person, possibly in a different channel') rather than 'this on-call member is an admin of this same workspace.'
issues.repair: Rewrite the selector as a single path where the admin filter is bound to the root: user_teams.team_id must equal teams.team_id (the same node/root as the origin), in addition to user_teams.user_id equaling the matched channel member. Remove the disconnected auxiliary existence check, or reformulate it so it references the same user variable produced by the focal join rather than an independent admin existence test.

issues.location: workspace_neg_summit outcome (T03SUMMIT) under the compiled selector
issues.problem: The Summit negative is specifically designed to test whether an admin role held in a different workspace should disqualify a match (per the binding_note's explicit counter-example). With the actual compiled query, Summit is excluded only because it coincidentally has zero admins anywhere in its own user_teams rows (auxiliary fails), not because the query correctly recognizes that Priyanka's admin role belongs to Northstar rather than Summit. If Summit had an unrelated admin in some other channel (not the on-call one), the flawed query would incorrectly classify Summit as a match, since the focal path only requires 'some on-call member is admin anywhere' and the auxiliary only requires 'workspace has some admin anywhere' — the intended near-miss scenario is not actually being tested by the mechanism the design claims to be testing.
issues.repair: After fixing the join to bind admin role to the same root workspace as described above, re-verify that Summit is excluded because Priyanka's admin association is tagged T02NORTHSTAR (not T03SUMMIT), which is the actual intended discriminator, not because of an unrelated absence of any admin in Summit.

rationale: The prompt, route, roles, seed edits, and bindings are otherwise coherent and well-differentiated (exact channel-name distractor, no-admin-at-all negative, split-record negative, cross-workspace-admin negative all present with plausible supporting data). However, the compiled query construction that is supposed to formally realize the binding_note's core requirement — that the SAME user must be both an on-call channel member and an admin of that SAME workspace — is not actually implemented: the focal and auxiliary paths are logically independent existence checks rather than a single relational condition tying the admin role to the same team_id as the root workspace and the same user_id as the channel member. The current seed happens to produce the intended matches/negatives by coincidence (Summit and the base workspace both happen to lack a real admin in the tested position for unrelated reasons), but this is exactly the kind of accidental-match risk and un-enforced same-record binding the review criteria instruct reviewers to catch ('Verify same-record bindings...', 'Code's query is a construction claim, not authority over the prompt'). This is a mechanical/query-construction defect that undermines the validity of the compiled artifact even though the natural-language design intent is sound, so the case should be sent back for a selector fix before compilation is accepted.
